title: New Rays CEO hosts meet-and-greet at Ferg's, says Trop will look 'better than it ever has' - NewsBreak
text:
By Marilyn Parker ,
1 hours ago
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (WFLA) — For the first time, one of the new owners of the Tampa Bay Rays spoke directly to fans of the team. A few dozen people packed out Ferg’s Sports Bar across the street from Tropicana Field to hear what he had to say.
“The Tampa Bay Rays have always called St. Petersburg home, and we cannot wait to be back at home in April,” said Ken Babby.
St. Petersburg residents allowed to stay in apartment units after failed fire inspections, new order says He told fans they’re about 145 days out from opening day. Babby said repairs to Tropicana Field are moving along.
“I think fans will see when they walk in in April that the Tropicana Field is going to look better than it ever has,” Babby said.
City leaders said as of Wednesday, just three more panels are needed to complete the roof, and work on the inside has started. The city said they don’t anticipate requesting any additional repair funds and they anticipate substantial completion of the city’s portion of the work at the end of February. Twenty-one of 24 roof panels are in place, panel No. 22 is scheduled to go up Thursday, No. 23 and No. 24 will go up next week.
Filling the stadium seats come April is another factor that Ferg’s owner Mark Ferguson discussed.
“I think we’re in a different place now than we were five, 10 years ago. We have a lot more people living in the area. We have a lot more businesses. And I think our support is going to show up this first year to show them how much we care about the Rays,” Ferguson said.
He said it was a hot and slow summer without the team at the Trop. Their business went down about 30%. Babby told fans he looks forward to bringing back business to Ferg’s and to the area next year.
In a memo Wednesday, St. Pete Mayor Ken Welch announced the city is extending the deadline to receive proposals for the Historic Gas Plant District. The 30-day notice will be published January 4, and proposals will be due February 3.
8 On Your Side asked Babby if they would be throwing their hat in that race.
“Yeah, we’re watching it just like everybody else says. We’ll see what the future brings. Obviously, this is an important site and we’re, you know, we’re working alongside and understanding all the aspects that go along with that,” Babby said.
A few proposals have already come in for the Historic Gas Plant District. Babby said they are doing feasibility studies on sites throughout the region for the future stadium.
“Tampa Bay Rays fans, the best is yet ahead. And we cannot wait to get started,” Babby said.
He celebrated by buying everyone at Ferg’s a beer.
Tickets for the Rays 2026 season go on sale Thursday.
